title: Three standout anime of 2026 worth watching
body_md:
The 2026 anime calendar has offered a wide range of new stories, including productions that stand out by exploring subjects rarely placed at the center of mainstream animation. A recommendation article published on November 26 highlights three particularly distinctive series. These selections represent an editorial assessment rather than an official ranking or a comprehensive audience poll.

## Smoking Behind the Supermarket With You

This twelve-episode first season approaches romance and companionship from an adult perspective. Sasaki, a man in his forties, develops a connection with a woman in her late twenties. The premise draws on the contrast between her friendly supermarket persona and the more relaxed, unconventional personality she displays outside the workplace.

Instead of relying on dramatic romantic declarations, the series finds interest in everyday conversations and the gradual development of trust. Its focus on adult routines, loneliness and companionship distinguishes it from many school-centered romance stories. Viewers looking for a quieter character-driven experience may find this an appealing alternative to more conventional romantic anime.

## Akane-banashi

Akane-banashi introduces viewers to rakugo, a traditional Japanese performance art centered on storytelling. Its protagonist, Akane, pursues recognition within a competitive artistic community where years of practice and the ability to engage an audience matter enormously.

The series uses the accessible structure of a competitive shonen story to explain an unfamiliar discipline. Training, rivalry and personal development become ways of exploring the craft rather than merely background details. The twelve-episode first season provides an introduction to both Akane's ambitions and the traditions surrounding her chosen profession. According to the recommendation article, another season is expected in winter 2027.

## Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia

Produced by Science SARU, this historical drama follows Sitara, whose experiences of loss initially motivate a quest for revenge against the Mongol Empire. As she becomes involved in the empire's internal affairs, the narrative develops into a more complicated exploration of political rivalry, loyalty and survival.

The story's shifting relationships make it difficult to classify every character as simply heroic or villainous. Sitara's priorities also evolve as she forms new attachments. Viewers who appreciate the political complexity of Game of Thrones may recognize a similar appeal in this historical setting, although the two productions are distinct works.

Together, these three series demonstrate the variety available in contemporary anime. Their strengths lie in different areas: intimate adult relationships, artistic competition and historical political intrigue. Choosing among them depends on the viewer's interests rather than accepting any single title as objectively superior to every other release of the year.
